### 7 Equilibria - Multiple Choice: Easy

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-easy-q1 data-answer="B"}
### Question 1 · Pressure and temperature · 1.7 Choice Easy Q1

For the equilibrium reaction $$\ce{N2O4(g) <=> 2NO2(g)}$$ which conditions give the greatest equilibrium yield of nitrogen dioxide?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>high pressure and low temperature</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>low pressure and high temperature</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>high pressure and high temperature</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>low pressure and low temperature</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> The forward reaction is endothermic and produces more gas moles, so high temperature and low pressure favour NO<sub>2</sub>.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-easy-q2 data-answer="B"}
### Question 2 · Contact process · 1.7 Choice Easy Q2

In the Contact process, $$\ce{2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g)}\qquad \Delta H=-197\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$$ Which statement is correct?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Increasing temperature increases the equilibrium yield of SO<sub>3</sub>.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Increasing temperature decreases the equilibrium yield of SO<sub>3</sub>.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>An iron catalyst changes the equilibrium position.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Increasing pressure decreases the equilibrium yield of SO<sub>3</sub>.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> The forward reaction is exothermic, so increasing temperature shifts equilibrium to the left. The industrial catalyst is vanadium(V) oxide and does not change the equilibrium position.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-easy-q3 data-answer="C"}
### Question 3 · Dynamic equilibrium · 1.7 Choice Easy Q3

Which statement describes a dynamic equilibrium?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>The forward reaction has stopped.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>The concentrations of reactants and products are equal.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>The forward and reverse reaction rates are equal in a closed system.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Only products are present.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Both reactions continue, but at equal rates; the concentrations therefore remain constant.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-easy-q4 data-answer="D"}
### Question 4 · Partial pressures · 1.7 Choice Easy Q4

For $$\ce{A(g) + B(g) <=> 2C(g)}$$ the total pressure is 3.0 atm. If the partial pressure of A is 0.50 atm and A and B have equal partial pressures, what is the partial pressure of C?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>0.50 atm</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>1.00 atm</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>1.50 atm</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>2.00 atm</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> The partial pressures of A and B total 1.0 atm, so C contributes 3.0−1.0=2.0 atm.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-easy-q5 data-answer="C"}
### Question 5 · Haber process equipment · 1.7 Choice Easy Q5

What is the purpose of the heat exchanger in the Haber process?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>It increases the temperature of the reacting gases.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>It removes nitrogen before the reaction.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>It cools the products and helps ammonia condense from unreacted gases.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>It changes the value of K<sub>c</sub>.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Hot products transfer heat to the incoming gases, then ammonia is cooled and separated while unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen are recycled.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-easy-q6 data-answer="C"}
### Question 6 · Ethanol manufacture · 1.7 Choice Easy Q6

Ethanol is manufactured by reacting steam with ethene:

$$\ce{C2H4(g) + H2O(g) <=> C2H5OH(g)}\qquad \Delta H=-45\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$$

Which changes would increase the equilibrium yield of ethanol?

1. Adding a catalyst.
2. Increasing the pressure.
3. Decreasing the temperature.

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>1 and 2</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>1 and 3</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>2 and 3</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>1, 2 and 3</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> The product side has fewer gas molecules and the forward reaction is exothermic. A catalyst changes rate, not equilibrium yield.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-easy-q7 data-answer="D"}
### Question 7 · Equilibrium constant and temperature · 1.7 Choice Easy Q7

Propyl ethanoate is formed in the esterification reaction:

$$\ce{propan-1-ol + ethanoic\ acid <=> propyl\ ethanoate + water}\qquad \Delta H=-10\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$$

How can the value of K<sub>c</sub> be increased?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Adding a catalyst</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Increasing pressure</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Increasing the concentration of an ester</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Decreasing temperature</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> For an exothermic forward reaction, lowering temperature favours products and increases K<sub>c</sub>. Pressure, concentration and catalysts do not change K<sub>c</sub>.</p></details>
:::

### 7 Equilibria - Multiple Choice: Medium

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-medium-q1 data-answer="A"}
### Question 8 · Calculating K<sub>c</sub> · 1.7 Choice Medium Q1

At 450 °C the value for K<sub>c</sub> for $$\ce{H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g)}$$ is 60. The equilibrium amounts of H<sub>2</sub> and I<sub>2</sub> are 2.0 mol and 0.30 mol, respectively. How many moles of HI are present at equilibrium in a 2 dm<sup>3</sup> vessel?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>6.0 mol dm<sup>−3</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>18 mol dm<sup>−3</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>36 mol dm<sup>−3</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>120 mol dm<sup>−3</sup></span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> $60=[\ce{HI}]^2/(2.0\times0.30)$, so [HI]=6.0 mol dm<sup>−3</sup>.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-medium-q2 data-answer="B"}
### Question 9 · Units of K<sub>c</sub> · 1.7 Choice Medium Q2

What are the units of K<sub>c</sub> for $$\ce{2CH4(g) <=> 3H2(g) + C2H2(g)}$$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>mol dm<sup>−3</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>mol<sup>2</sup> dm<sup>−6</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>mol<sup>−2</sup> dm<sup>6</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>no units</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> The total power of concentration is 4−2=2, giving mol<sup>2</sup> dm<sup>−6</sup>.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-medium-q3 data-answer="A"}
### Question 10 · K<sub>p</sub> · 1.7 Choice Medium Q3

For $$\ce{N2O4(g) <=> 2NO2(g)}$$ the equilibrium partial pressures are p(N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>) = 0.33 atm and p(NO<sub>2</sub>) = 0.67 atm. What is K<sub>p</sub>?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>1.36 atm</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>0.49 atm</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>0.22 atm</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>0.074 atm</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> $K_p=p(\ce{NO2})^2/p(\ce{N2O4})=0.67^2/0.33=1.36$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-medium-q4 data-answer="D"}
### Question 11 · Equilibrium composition · 1.7 Choice Medium Q4

Nitrogen monoxide and oxygen can be formed from the thermal decomposition of nitrogen dioxide:

$$\ce{2NO2(g) <=> 2NO(g) + O2(g)}$$

In an experiment 4.0 mol of nitrogen dioxide are put into a 1 dm<sup>3</sup> container. The equilibrium mixture contains 0.8 mol of oxygen. What is the value of K<sub>c</sub>?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$0.87\times0.8/4^2$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$1.6\times0.8/2.4^2$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$1.67\times0.8/2.4^2$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$1.6^2\times0.8/2.4^2$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> At equilibrium [NO<sub>2</sub>] = 2.4, [NO] = 1.6 and [O<sub>2</sub>] = 0.8 mol dm<sup>−3</sup>. Thus $K_c=(1.6^2\times0.8)/(2.4^2)$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-medium-q5 data-answer="C"}
### Question 12 · Contact process stages · 1.7 Choice Medium Q5

Which statement about the Contact process is correct?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>All three stages are reversible.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>All three stages are endothermic.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>The oxidation of sulfur dioxide is reversible and exothermic.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>The catalyst increases the equilibrium yield of sulfur trioxide.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Sulfur dioxide is oxidised to sulfur trioxide in the reversible, exothermic middle stage; the catalyst only increases rate.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-medium-q6 data-answer="B"}
### Question 13 · Temperature, pressure and volume · 1.7 Choice Medium Q6

For a dissociation reaction in which the forward reaction is endothermic and produces more gas molecules, what happens when temperature is increased at constant pressure?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Equilibrium shifts left and volume decreases.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Equilibrium shifts right and volume increases.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Equilibrium shifts left and volume increases.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Equilibrium shifts right and volume decreases.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> Higher temperature favours the endothermic direction. At constant pressure, the increased temperature also causes thermal expansion.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-medium-q7 data-answer="B"}
### Question 14 · Strong and weak acids · 1.7 Choice Medium Q7

Solutions P and Q each have concentration 2.0 mol dm<sup>−3</sup>. P has pH 9 and Q has pH 6. Which statement is correct?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Q is a strong acid.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Q has a lower percentage dissociation than P.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>P has a higher hydrogen-ion concentration than Q.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>P and Q must be the same acid.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> P is alkaline and Q is acidic. At the same formal concentration, a weak acid has a smaller percentage dissociation than a weak base can have in the corresponding comparison.</p></details>
:::

### 7 Equilibria - Multiple Choice: Hard

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-hard-q1 data-answer="D"}
### Question 15 · K<sub>2</sub>O titration · 1.7 Choice Hard Q1

Use of the periodic table is relevant to this question. A sample of potassium oxide, K<sub>2</sub>O, is dissolved in 500 cm<sup>3</sup> of distilled water. 25.0 cm<sup>3</sup> of this solution is titrated against sulfuric acid of concentration 1.5 mol dm<sup>−3</sup>. 20.0 cm<sup>3</sup> of sulfuric acid is needed for complete neutralisation. What is the mass of potassium oxide originally dissolved in 500 cm<sup>3</sup> of distilled water?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>2.83 g</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>28.3 g</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>47.1 g</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>56.6 g</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> In 20.0 cm<sup>3</sup>, $n(\ce{H2SO4})=1.5\times0.0200=0.0300$ mol, so the 25.0 cm<sup>3</sup> portion contains 0.0600 mol KOH. The 500 cm<sup>3</sup> solution therefore contains 1.20 mol KOH and 0.600 mol K<sub>2</sub>O. Its mass is approximately $0.600\times94=56.6$ g.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-hard-q2 data-answer="D"}
### Question 16 · Methanol equilibrium · 1.7 Choice Hard Q2

For $$\ce{CO(g) + 2H2(g) <=> CH3OH(g)}$$ a dynamic equilibrium is set up in a 2 dm<sup>3</sup> sealed vessel. At equilibrium there are 6.20×10<sup>−3</sup> mol CO, 4.80×10<sup>−3</sup> mol H<sub>2</sub> and 5.20×10<sup>−5</sup> mol CH<sub>3</sub>OH. Where has the equilibrium shifted, and what is the value of K<sub>c</sub>?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>To the right, K<sub>c</sub> = 364</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>To the left, K<sub>c</sub> = 364</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>To the left, K<sub>c</sub> = 14.56</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>To the right, K<sub>c</sub> = 14.56</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> Substituting concentrations into $K_c=[\ce{CH3OH}]/([\ce{CO}][\ce{H2}]^2)$ gives approximately 14.6; the small methanol amount reflects the starting composition and stoichiometry, not a K<sub>c</sub> below 1.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-hard-q3 data-answer="C"}
### Question 17 · Percentage yield · 1.7 Choice Hard Q3

Gaseous reactants A and B react to form gaseous product C in a 3:2 ratio in a 5 dm<sup>3</sup> container. In an experiment, 1.0 mol of A and 1.0 mol of B are used. At equilibrium, only 10% of A has reacted. What is the equilibrium concentration of C?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>0.010 mol dm<sup>−3</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>0.020 mol dm<sup>−3</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>0.040 mol dm<sup>−3</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>0.200 mol dm<sup>−3</sup></span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> 0.10 mol A reacts and forms 0.20 mol C. Dividing by 5.0 dm<sup>3</sup> gives 0.040 mol dm<sup>−3</sup>.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-hard-q4 data-answer="A"}
### Question 18 · Oxygen binding · 1.7 Choice Hard Q4

For $$\ce{Hb + 4O2 <=> Hb(O2)4}$$ the equilibrium concentrations of Hb and Hb(O<sub>2</sub>)<sub>4</sub> are equal. If [O<sub>2</sub>] = 6.7×10<sup>−6</sup> mol dm<sup>−3</sup>, what is K<sub>c</sub>?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>5×10<sup>20</sup> dm<sup>12</sup> mol<sup>−4</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>2×10<sup>−5</sup> dm<sup>12</sup> mol<sup>−4</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>1.5×10<sup>5</sup> dm<sup>3</sup> mol<sup>−1</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>6.7×10<sup>−6</sup> dm<sup>3</sup> mol<sup>−1</sup></span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> $K_c=[\ce{Hb(O2)4}]/([\ce{Hb}][\ce{O2}]^4)=1/[\ce{O2}]^4$, which is approximately 5×10<sup>20</sup>.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-hard-q5 data-answer="B"}
### Question 19 · Solids omitted from K<sub>c</sub> · 1.7 Choice Hard Q5

An aqueous solution contains 1.0 mol silver nitrate and 1.0 mol iron(II) sulfate in a 2.00 dm<sup>3</sup> container. At equilibrium there are 0.44 mol silver ions:

$$\ce{Ag+(aq) + Fe^{2+}(aq) <=> Ag(s) + Fe^{3+}(aq)}$$

What is the numerical value of K<sub>c</sub>?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>579</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>5.79 mol<sup>−1</sup> dm<sup>3</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>1.27 mol<sup>−1</sup> dm<sup>3</sup></span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>1.27</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> At equilibrium [Ag<sup>+</sup>] = [Fe<sup>2+</sup>] = 0.44/2.00 and [Fe<sup>3+</sup>] = 0.56/2.00 mol dm<sup>−3</sup>. Pure silver is omitted, giving $K_c=5.79\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}\ dm^3}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #equilibria-choice-hard-q6 data-answer="C"}
### Question 20 · Haber process calculation · 1.7 Choice Hard Q6

In the Haber process, 560 kg of nitrogen and 120 kg of hydrogen are mixed. At equilibrium, 96 kg of hydrogen remains. What mass of ammonia is formed?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>4.53×10<sup>4</sup> g</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>9.07×10<sup>4</sup> g</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>1.36×10<sup>5</sup> g</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>2.72×10<sup>5</sup> g</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Hydrogen consumed is 24 kg = 12 000 mol. From $\ce{N2: H2: NH3}=1:3:2$, ammonia formed is 8000 mol = 136 000 g.</p></details>
:::
